hypothesis: If the claim holds, when all 4096 two-state two-colour Turing machines are run under the book's one-sided convention on every input x with up to 10 binary digits, the maximum halting time T(n) over inputs of length n is, for every machine (and every distinct function/time pair), either constant, linear, quadratic or exponential in n, and every function computed with exponential T(n) is also computed by some two-state two-colour machine with constant T(n).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Conventions from NKS pp. 761 and 1143: tape cells i = 1, 2, ... hold the binary digits of x with the least significant digit at i = 1 (x = 0 is the single digit 0), all other cells 0; head starts at i = 1 in state 1; a step applies the rule (new state, new colour, displacement d) and moves the head to i - d; the computation is complete at the first step t at which i = 0; the output f(x) is the tape read as a binary number. Machines are numbered with the NKS scheme (p. 888). Inputs x = 0..1023 (lengths n = 1..10). Non-halting is established by (i) a cycle of states that keeps moving left on blank cells once the head is left of every visited cell, (ii) exact repetition of the configuration (Brent's algorithm), or (iii) a cutoff of 20000 steps. For each machine and each distinct (f, t) pair over x = 0..1023, T(n) = max t(x) over halting x of length n. Growth class on n = 3..10, requiring halting inputs at >= 5 of these lengths (otherwise 'insufficient'): exact fit (max residual < 1e-9) tried in the order constant, linear a+bn (b>0), quadratic a+bn+cn^2 (c>0), exponential a*2^n+b (a>0); if none is exact, the lowest-complexity of linear, quadratic, exponential (a*c^n+b, c in {2,3,4}) whose relative RMS residual over n = 3..10 is <= 0.15; else 'other'. PASS (supports) if (a) no (f, t) pair with sufficient data is classed 'other', and (b) for every exponential pair the same function f (as a map on x = 0..1023 including where it is undefined) is computed by at least one machine whose pair is classed constant. The book's census numbers (748 never halt / 3348 sometimes / 1683 always; 351 functions, 149 total; 492 (f,t) pairs; 164 constant, 295 linear, 27 quadratic, 6 exponential; machines 378, 1953, 2289 exponential with total functions; the formulas for machines 3279, 1285, 3333, 261, 1447, 1953, 1969, 3517, 3246, 3374) are recorded as cross-checks of the implementation and do not decide the verdict.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. FAIL (refutes) if some (f, t) pair with sufficient data has a growth class other than constant, linear, quadratic or exponential and this is confirmed when the machine is rerun on x up to 2^14 - 1 with cutoff 2^20 steps (e.g. a cubic or super-exponential fit is best), or if some exponential pair has no constant-time partner computing the same function. MIXED if 'other' pairs exist but on the extended inputs fit one of the four classes within tolerance, or if the cross-check numbers disagree with the book in a way that indicates a convention mismatch.
interpretation: The claim is a census statement under a specific computational convention (head leaves the right end), which the book's notes state precisely and which is implemented literally. 'Rate of growth' is finite-sample: classes are assigned from n = 3..10 by exact or near-exact fits, which cannot prove asymptotics but follow the book's own method of reading growth from short inputs. 'The same function' is tested on the same finite input range including the halting/non-halting pattern.

datasets.name: All 4096 two-state two-colour Turing machines (NKS numbering) run on inputs 0..1023 under the one-sided halting convention of NKS p. 761, generated by analysis.py

generator.program_family: s = 2 states, k = 2 colours, rule (state, colour) -> (new state, new colour, displacement), NKS numbering p. 888
generator.inputs: x = 0..1023 as binary digits, least significant at cell 1 (head start), tape extends to the left
generator.halting: head moves to cell 0; non-halting by blank-left state cycle, configuration repetition, or 20000-step cutoff
generator.output: tape contents read as a binary number
generator.growth_fit: lengths n = 3..10, exact fits then relative RMS <= 0.15

datasets.role: the computational objects the claim is about
